authority: #K2-468 sec.3.4: when the precheck still FAILS, the NAMED list is the scheme-layer input. This census turns "no escape" into "blocked by WHOM, in WHICH direction" - read-only, bounded (8 directions x 20 steps x local obstacles; 0.34s wall clock).

interpretation.U1_pad22: I2C2_SCL @ (37.75,57.1625) on F.Cu: every one of the 8 directions is first-blocked by GND (the nearest foreign object in each ray is GND copper/pads). So this pad sits inside a GND-dense neighbourhood and has no free ray within the 2.0mm / 0.30mm criterion - independent of direction choice.
interpretation.I2C1_SDA_pad: I2C1_SDA @ (33.25,48.8375) on F.Cu: the nearest blocker is I2C1_SCL (0.4mm) in the E/NE rays and an unnamed pad (net="") in the others - i.e. a tightly packed pin field, not a pour.
interpretation.caveat_READ_THIS: DISTANCES ARE APPROXIMATE IN THIS CENSUS: pads are modelled as POINTS with half their size (the same permissive model used by the planner), so the per-direction "first contact" identifies the NEAREST FOREIGN OBJECT ROBUSTLY but its distance is only indicative. For a scheme-layer decision, the pad TRUE SHAPES must be used.
interpretation.what_it_means: neither refusal is an artifact of the direction set or of the candidate ladder: even the extended set (8 dirs + dogleg, 560 candidates) finds nothing, and the census shows the pads are hemmed in from every side. The choice is therefore a SCHEME-LAYER one: (A) re-derive the escape criterion from the product practice (TI EVM / SNLA425 / IPC-7351 - anchors already in REF-CASE-LIBRARY sec.E), or (B) give these two pads explicit exits/relocations in the drawing.
